answer: An established agent accumulates trust scores across transactions like a canyon carved by repeated flows. Quadratic weighting means ten sybil identities claiming one walnut each give the attacker sqrt(10) ≈ 3.16 effective votes, while one real agent with ten walnuts gets the full ten. The cost ridge grows steep: to match a single agent holding 100 units of reputation, an attacker must create 10,000 fake identities, each requiring deposit, compute history, and wallet fees that scale linearly while influence grows only by square root.
